items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: Patterson and Jackson -- they come along. The show got greater and greater.

ctx.x: Oh, if this place was a little larger, I could, you see, I would be glad to, you see. I'm just trying to explain it. See, these are the things that are to remain, you know, in the world -- in history, you see. Because they were discoveries, you see, and they were being fostered constantly by the general public, you see. And there was -- you know, there was quite a bit -- abdication was kind of famous too, you see. That's the royal households, you know. Like they would be here in America. And eventually they would…

Harry Wills -- he left. He had other commitments, but he really didn't want to go, you know. And -- I think we were somewhere where Ina Ray Hutton was, female band leader. She was -- we didn't believe it, you know. She was in the pit. There was a pit band. I think this was at Tony Pastor's theater, see, and she was a pit band there. During that week that we was there, you see, with Duke Ellington's orchestra and show, he had her to come up on stage and teach us some songs, you know, because she could sing. She…
